1	# LOOM portal: interface for agents
2	
3	This page is for an agent (or the developer of one) that needs part of a
4	person's health context to do a task for them. It is the only document an
5	agent needs; it does not have to read LOOM's source.
6	
7	## What LOOM offers
8	
9	LOOM holds one person's health record and hands out **task-scoped,
10	expiring slices** of it. You say what task you are doing; LOOM decides
11	how deep you may see, which fields you get, and for how long.
12	
13	| Tier | What it contains | Field names |
14	|---|---|---|
15	| L0 | raw sensor signal | `raw_signal` |
16	| L1 | readings (here: hourly glucose, mg/dL) | `readings` |
17	| L2 | patterns and alerts derived from readings | `glucose_patterns`, `alerts` |
18	| L3 | plain-language constraints | `constraints` |
19	
20	L0 is the deepest (most revealing), L3 the shallowest. A tier includes the
21	shallower ones: an L2 grant may carry `constraints` too.
22	
23	## Access
24	
25	- Base URL and namespace are given to you by whoever runs the portal (for
26	  a test: `http://127.0.0.1:8787` and a namespace such as `demo`).
27	  Every call for one person goes to `/v1/<namespace>/...`.
28	- There is no login in v0.1. You identify yourself with `agent_id` (this
29	  agent instance) and `publisher` (the company or developer that ships
30	  it). In Nanda Town the gateway fills `agent_id` from the signed envelope;
31	  over plain HTTP both are claims.
32	- JSON in, JSON out. Errors are JSON `{"error": "..."}`; a malformed body
33	  gets HTTP 400 naming the missing fields.
34	
35	## Endpoints
36	
37	| Method and path | Use |
38	|---|---|
39	| `GET /health` | version and policy id |
40	| `POST /v1/<ns>/requests` | ask for access for a task; a grant carries data immediately |
41	| `POST /v1/<ns>/fetch` | get fresh data again under a grant you already hold |
42	| `GET /v1/<ns>/credit` | publisher → credit score (only publishers that have been seen) |
43	| `GET /v1/<ns>/log` | the person's audit log: every decision, without the data (owner token only; agents get 403) |
44	| `GET /v1/policy` | the built-in tasks, as JSON (same as the table below) |
45	| `GET /v1/<ns>/proposals/<proposal_id>` | status of a proposal for a task that is not built in (see below) |
46	
47	### `POST /v1/<ns>/requests`: body
48	
49	| Field | Required | Meaning |
50	|---|---|---|
51	| `request_id` | yes | unique per request; reuse it only to retry the same request |
52	| `agent_id` | yes | your agent instance |
53	| `publisher` | yes | who ships you |
54	| `category` | yes | `agent_for_user` (works for the person) or `care_provider` (clinician side) |
55	| `task` | yes | one of the task names below |
56	| `purpose` | no | free text, recorded |
57	| `tier` | yes | the deepest tier you ask for (`L0`..`L3`) |
58	| `fields` | yes | list of field names you ask for |
59	| `at` | yes | current time on the person's timeline, in days (number) |
60	
61	### Tasks (policy `loom-policy-0.2.1`)
62	
63	| `task` | `category` | Deep

mkdir -p /home/claude/hw9-coldstart/run3/out && cat > /home/claude/hw9-coldstart/run3/out/clinic-1.md <<'EOF'
# Pre-visit summary: diabetes clinic appointment (tomorrow, day 1)

Prepared by `clinic-1` (publisher `cambridge-clinic`) on day 0 from the patient's LOOM portal (namespace `coldstart-3`). The record is synthetic.

> **Before use:** LOOM returned `confirmation: first_request` for this grant. The patient has to confirm this first use of their data before the clinic acts on it. LOOM reports that requirement but doesn't collect the confirmation, so the front desk or clinician should get it, for example at check-in.

## Glucose over the last 14 days (CGM-derived patterns)

| Metric | Value | Comment |
|---|---|---|
| Mean glucose | 127 mg/dL | Equals an estimated GMI of about 6.3% (computed from the mean, not a lab A1c) |
| Glucose variability (CV) | 14.8% | Well under the 36% stability threshold |
| Time in range | 100% | LOOM doesn't state the range; presumably 70–180 mg/dL |
| Post-meal peak | 177 mg/dL | Just under 180 mg/dL |
| Hypoglycaemia | None flagged | No low alerts in the window; 100% TIR implies no time below 70 mg/dL |

## Alerts

- **Post-meal spikes: 15 in 14 days**, about one a day. This is the only alert type. Peaks stay below 180 mg/dL, so the spikes don't push readings out of range. Still, they're the main pattern worth discussing.

## Patient's stated constraints

- Limit added sugar
- Prefer low-glycaemic foods

## Suggested discussion points

1. **Post-meal excursions.** Ask which meals and foods cause the daily spikes and when they happen. Check whether they match what the patient already tries to do (low-GI, limited added sugar). Consider meal timing, portion size, a walk after meals, or a referral for dietary review.
2. **Overall control looks good.** Mean, CV and TIR are all at target. Reinforce the current regimen; there's no sign of hypoglycaemia risk in this data.
3. **Things to confirm in person** (not available from LOOM): current medications and doses, a recent lab A1c, diabetes type, weight/BP, the patient's own goals, and what range LOOM uses for TIR and what it counts as a "spike".

## Limits of this summary

- It covers derived patterns only (L2). No hourly readings were requested, so I can't say what time of day or after which meal the spikes happen.
- 14 days of data from one source, with no medication, lab or history data.
- GMI is an estimate calculated from mean glucose. It doesn't replace an A1c.

## What I got from LOOM and how I used it

- **Request:** one `POST /v1/coldstart-3/requests`, category `care_provider`, task `clinical_visit` (the built-in task for clinic-side visit prep), tier `L2`, fields `glucose_patterns`, `alerts`, `constraints`, `at: 0`. That's exactly what the task allows. I didn't ask for raw signal or hourly readings (L0/L1), because the task doesn't permit them and a one-page summary doesn't need them.
- **Decision:** `granted` (`task_basis`), grant `g-1456dbfd25`, valid 14 days (expires day 14), not single-use. Publisher credit went from 60 to 61 (medium band). Friction: `confirmation: first_request`, `auto_renew: false`.
- **Data received:** `glucose_patterns` (14-day window: mean 127 mg/dL, CV 14.8%, post-meal peak 177 mg/dL, TIR 100%); `alerts` (`post_meal_spike` × 15); `constraints` (`limit_added_sugar`, `prefer_low_glycemic`).
- **How I used it:** the patterns became the metrics table (plus a GMI estimate I calculated from the mean). The alert became the main discussion point. The constraints were used as context for dietary counselling. No other data sources were used. I made no further fetches; the grant can be fetched again until day 14 if the clinic needs fresher numbers on the visit day.
EOF

input.message: The pre-visit summary is written to /home/claude/hw9-coldstart/run3/out/clinic-1.md. I made one request to LOOM as a clinic (`care_provider`) for the built-in `clinical_visit` task, at tier L2, asking only for the three fields that task allows: `glucose_patterns`, `alerts` and `constraints`, at day 0. LOOM granted it (grant g-1456dbfd25, valid until day 14, publisher credit 60 to 61). The person's 14-day numbers look well controlled: mean glucose 127 mg/dL (about 6.3% GMI, which I estimated from the mean myself), CV 14.8%, time in range 100%, post-meal peak 177 mg/dL and no lows flagged. The only alert is 15 post-meal spikes in 14 days, about one a day, so the summary makes post-meal excursions the main thing to discuss, along with the person's stated preferences (limit added sugar, prefer low-glycaemic foods). The summary lists what LOOM can't provide and the clinic should confirm in person: medications, a lab A1c, the TIR range LOOM uses and how it defines a spike. Without hourly readings I can't say when the spikes happen. It also flags that LOOM returned `confirmation: first_request`, which means the person has to confirm this first use of their data before the clinic acts on it. LOOM doesn't collect that confirmation itself, so the clinic will need to get it. The file ends with the required section "What I got from LOOM and how I used it". I didn't read any other files or make further fetches.
